lines.text: When I opened my door on my return, Flush threw himself upon me with a most ecstatical agony, and for full ten minutes did not cease jumping and kissing my hands—he thought he had lost me for certain, this time.
lines.note: Flush's ecstatic welcome shows Elizabeth's tenderness and the life Robert is entering.

lines.text: You have heard all I can say ... say you, shall I come to-morrow?
lines.note: Robert asks whether he may come, showing early caution and devotion.

lines.text: But if one heart and one life will do, ... they are yours ...
lines.note: Elizabeth gives her heart and life to him entirely.

lines.text: I have just come from the vestry of Paddington chapel, and bore it very well, and saw nobody except one woman.
lines.note: Elizabeth succeeds at the vestry after earlier church panic.

lines.text: Here is a distress for me, dearest!
lines.note: Flush is stolen, turning a private worry into real peril.

lines.text: It seems to me that you and I are at one upon the whole question,—only that I am your Flush, and he is mine.
lines.note: Elizabeth reframes their Flush dispute as mutual protection.

lines.text: Only a few words to tell you that Flush is found, and lying on the sofa, with one paw and both ears hanging over the edge of it.
lines.note: Flush returns home, exhausted but safe.

lines.text: We must be married directly and go to Italy.
lines.note: Robert insists they must marry and leave at once.

lines.text: I look back, and in every one point, every word and gesture, every letter, every silence—you have been entirely perfect to me—I would not change one word, one look.
lines.note: Robert looks back and calls every moment perfect.

lines.text: All that I am, I owe you—if I enjoy anything now and henceforth, it is through you.
lines.note: Elizabeth says all she is she owes to him.

lines.text: And the dear, dear little bud!—I shall keep it to the end of my life, if you love me so long, ... or not, sir!
lines.note: Robert's bud becomes a keepsake Elizabeth will treasure.

lines.text: By to-morrow at this time, I shall have you only, to love me—my beloved!
lines.note: Elizabeth anticipates having only him to love.
